pre_change_state.caveat_quote: I searched until I hit the tool limit, so this map is wide but not exhaustive.

claims.text: **Responses vary a lot.** People respond very differently, and those with less impairment tend to benefit more [W2778691880], [W2732925385].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: W2778691880 reports considerable variation in responses to PARO, and W2732925385 reports that care recipients with less cognitive impairment responded significantly better, so each part is supported by its cited paper.
claims.first_rationale: Only W2732925385 reports that less-impaired people respond better; W2778691880 reports variation in responses but not that less impairment benefits more.

claims.text: Other systems: [W3089483243], [W2793187533], [W2025048472], [W2731113721] (walking guidance), and partner-dance robot acceptance [W2766970278].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: The descriptions match: exercise/robot systems, walking guidance (W2731113721), partner-dance acceptance (W2766970278).

claims.text: **Banks et al., AIBO and loneliness [W2132164645]:** long-term care residents; dementia not mentioned in the abstract
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Banks et al. studied LTCF residents and loneliness with AIBO; the abstract does not mention dementia.

claims.text: Acceptability of animal-like robots for people with early dementia [W2159536297]
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: The paper addresses acceptability of animaloid robots by older people with early dementia.

claims.text: Improvements in communication, self-care and social life against care-plan targets based on the WHO's ICF framework [W2898061611].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Improvements in communication, self care and social life with ICF-based targets are in the abstract.

claims.text: The NAO group declined on the MMSE (a standard cognitive test) [W1807810766].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: The NAO group showed MMSE decline in Phase 1.

claims.text: **Home settings are barely studied.** Only three kept studies involve the home: [W2732925385] (partly), [W3034490183] and [W1994379356].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: W2732925385 includes home use, W3034490183 is a home study, and W1994379356 is home-based care; the 'only three' is a claim about the assistant's kept set, and the cited papers do involve the home.

claims.text: An early Japanese study reported quality-of-life gains [W382502046].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: The 2002 Japanese AIBO study reported QOL improvements.

claims.text: [W2294211165]:** dementia diagnoses were recorded, but having dementia wasn't required to take part
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: The abstract says dementia diagnoses were collected as data, not that dementia was required.

claims.text: PARO turned on vs off in occupational therapy [W4407738599]
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: The paper concerns PARO versus a stuffed animal in occupational therapy, with PARO described as interactive; 'turned on vs off' is a title-based paraphrase.

claims.text: People with less cognitive impairment responded better [W2732925385].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Subanalyses showed less-impaired recipients responded significantly better.

claims.text: Private-home studies are fewer, smaller and more technology-focused [W2994761079], [W2717439789].
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: The records give no basis for comparing the number or size of private-home studies or calling them more technology-focused.

claims.text: Others I found but didn't open: [W2000476293], [W2154543439], [W2888482633], [W2751864896] (telepresence robots in dementia), [W2586081748] (qualitative evidence), [W2999297198] (barriers to implementing humanoid robots).
claims.label: not_a_claim
claims.rationale: A list of papers the assistant did not open, with brief topic labels.

claims.text: **Comparison conditions matter.** Against a live dog or a plush toy, robots often perform similarly to the alternative, so the specific value of the robot is unclear [W2294211165], [W2132164645], [W2778691880].
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: The papers do not show robots performing similarly to live dogs or plush toys; several show robots stimulating more interaction or improvement than controls.

claims.text: **Effect modifiers:** Severity of dementia [W2732925385], [W1505024467] and individual variability [W2778691880].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: W2732925385 and W1505024467 address cognitive impairment or dementia severity differences, and W2778691880 addresses individual variability.

claims.text: Snippet only: meal-time assistance [W2112421347], acceptance study [W2046365492], Tangy running Bingo [W2602852930]
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Meal-time assistance, acceptance study and Bingo (Tangy) match the three records.

claims.text: Three months of naturalistic observation with PARO in a public area of a nursing home [W2039822570].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: A three-month field study with PARO in a public area of a nursing home is stated.

claims.text: A childlike companion robot with residents with dementia [W3111679151]
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: The paper studied residents with cognitive impairment, not specifically dementia.

claims.text: | Fasola & Matarić exercise coach [W1967507142] | Older adults in general (n = 33) |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Fasola & Matarić exercise coach with older adults, n=33.

claims.text: | Hobbit, earlier report [W3137166629] *(snippet)* | Older adults in 18 private homes |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: The earlier Hobbit report was deployed in 18 private households of older adults.

claims.text: **Customisable robot dog [W2883046174]** *(snippet)*: nursing home residents
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: A customizable robot dog with nursing home residents matches the title and abstract.

claims.text: AIBO stimulated as much social interaction as a live dog, with longer looks and more conversation started by residents [W1972564462].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: AIBO stimulated more than the visitor alone, with longer looks and more resident-initiated conversation than the live dog; 'as much as a live dog' is a loose paraphrase.

claims.text: Face scales and the Geriatric Depression Scale suggested improved mood [W2148142846].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Face scales and GDS were used and feelings improved.

claims.text: **Sunshine chat robot [W3041860695]:** "cognitive impairment," not necessarily dementia
claims.label: not_a_claim
claims.rationale: The abstract is truncated and gives no content; the statement is a note about the assistant's own reading and the wording, not an assertion about the paper.

claims.text: Early acceptability study in early dementia [W2159536297]
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Preliminary acceptability study in older subjects with mild cognitive deficits (MMSE>23).

claims.text: | Chen et al. 2018, *J Nursing Scholarship* [W2889960145] | 7 studies on depression | 3 found reduced depressive symptoms; 3 found non-significant downward trends. Not strong enough for clinical recommendations. |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Matches: 7 studies, three promising, three non-significant trends, evidence not strong enough.

claims.text: **Matilda** [W1994379356] *(snippet)*: a socially assistive robot delivering services to people with dementia in home-based care in Australia.
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Matilda is a socially assistive robot for PwD in home-based care in Australia.

claims.text: How people with mild-to-moderate dementia see PARO in relation to pain and mood [W2985514812] *(snippet)*
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Matches the qualitative study of PARO, pain and mood in mild to moderate dementia.

claims.text: Standardised scales for depression, quality of life, agitation and cognition often don't move [W2808281222], [W2955051104], [W1945345301].
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: W1945345301 is not in the records, and the other papers do not clearly show scales often fail to move, including cognition.

claims.text: Implementation questions: staff workload, infection control [W3081435517], ethics of deception and withdrawal [W2778691880], and cost.
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: W3081435517 is not in the records, and W2778691880 does not discuss ethics of deception and withdrawal; it discusses individual responses and ethics of giving and retrieving PARO, so the claim is incomplete.

claims.text: Related papers on views of people with dementia and other stakeholders, and on loneliness: [W3105249390], [W2896071495], [W2889731820]
claims.label: not_a_claim
claims.rationale: A bare list of ids with a generic description.

claims.text: **Taiwan PARO study:** older adults with depression [W3015603533]
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: W3015603533 is not among the records shown.

claims.text: an apathy pilot in long-term care [W3113108394]
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: W3113108394 is not among the records shown.

claims.text: **NAO theatre interventions** [W2982896790], [W2899915867] *(snippets)*: older adults in residential care
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: W2982896790 and W2899915867 are not among the records shown.

claims.text: [W2132164645] and an early Japanese study [W382502046], both with general long-term care residents
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Both are about general long-term care residents; Banks in LTCF and the Japanese study with elderly patients.

claims.text: PARO in group sensory therapy in a nursing home [W2040979576], [W4243437205].
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: W2040979576 and W4243437205 are not among the records shown.

claims.text: dogs versus robotic animals for nursing home residents with dementia [W2946010724]
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: W2946010724 is not among the records shown.

claims.text: | Robot-administered cognitive tests [W2924547041] *(snippet)* | Older adults living in the community |
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: W2924547041 is not among the records shown.

claims.text: | Moyle et al. 2013 [W1488883230] | 1 Australian facility, 18 residents with mid- to late-stage dementia | Pilot randomised crossover; PARO vs reading group | Moderate-to-large improvement in quality of life; more pleasure |
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: W1488883230 is not among the records shown.

claims.text: **Hong Kong PARO study [W2080233792]:** "declining cognitive function," which may not mean diagnosed dementia.
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: W2080233792 is not among the records shown.
